Iron Deficiency Anaemia.description: Iron deficiency anaemia is the most common type of anaemia in children, caused by insufficient iron in the body to produce hemoglobin. It can significantly impact a child's physical and cognitive development.
treatments: Iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate or ferrous fumarate)
Iron-rich diet including lean meats, fish, poultry, beans, and fortified cereals
Vitamin C supplementation to enhance iron absorption
Treatment of any underlying causes (parasites, blood loss)
Regular blood tests to monitor iron levels

Kwashiorkor.description: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of protein-energy malnutrition characterized by edema, skin changes, and hair changes. It typically occurs when a child's diet is severely deficient in protein but may have adequate calories.
treatments: Immediate medical attention and hospitalization if severe

Marasmus.description: Marasmus is a severe form of protein-energy malnutrition characterized by chronic wasting of body tissues. It results from a severe deficiency of both calories and protein, leading to extreme weight loss and muscle wasting.
treatments: Carefully planned refeeding program to prevent refeeding syndrome
Therapeutic milk formula (F-75, F-100) in controlled amounts
Treatment of underlying infections and complications

Vitamin A Deficiency.description: Vitamin A deficiency is a common micronutrient deficiency that can lead to night blindness, increased susceptibility to infections, and in severe cases, blindness. It's particularly common in areas with limited access to vitamin A-rich foods.
treatments: Diet rich in vitamin A sources (orange vegetables, leafy greens, liver)
Regular monitoring of vitamin A levels
